project_scope.note: Canonical Verbena species remain photo-light; rights-cleared Lantana family references supply fruit/head breadth until Verbena images are locked.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with opposite/decussate exstipulate leaves, then the inflorescence: spikes or compact heads are common. Confirm a tubular flower, superior ovary and usually terminal style.
family_diagnostics.flowers: Usually 4- or 5-merous, tubular and zygomorphic to weakly bilabiate.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Can split into 2 or 4 mericarps or become drupaceous, depending on genus.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Square stems and aroma do not separate Verbenaceae from Lamiaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → high-value structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: The family lesson is really about inflorescence + style/ovary/fruit, not 'square stem versus mint.'

steps.title: 1 · Keep the Verbena spike in mind
steps.look_for: Opposite leaves and an elongated spike of small tubular flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the common local Verbena family form.

steps.title: 2 · Add capitate family breadth
steps.look_for: Woody habit with opposite rough leaves and dense rounded flower heads.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows that Verbenaceae is broader than Verbena spikes.

steps.title: 3 · See the drupaceous exception
steps.look_for: Fleshy dark drupe-like fruit rather than four dry mericarps.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents memorizing one fruit type for the family.

steps.title: 4 · Separate from Lamiaceae
steps.look_for: Verbenaceae commonly has a terminal style and less deeply lobed ovary; Lamiaceae commonly has a deeply 4-lobed ovary with gynobasic style.
steps.why_it_matters: This is far stronger than stem shape.

comparisons.title: Verbenaceae vs Lamiaceae
comparisons.rule: Do not use square stems alone. Read inflorescence architecture, ovary lobing, style position and fruit.

comparisons.title: Verbenaceae vs Rubiaceae
comparisons.rule: Rubiaceae has interpetiolar stipules and an inferior ovary; Verbenaceae lacks stipules and has a superior ovary.

visual_lesson.caveat: The canonical Verbena photo lock is still pending; the current visual module is scientifically usable but not visually complete.

family_confusion_cleanup.field_question: Opposite leaves and a tubular flower: mint, verbena, or madder/coffee family?
look_here_first: At the node: are there interpetiolar stipules between opposite leaves?
At the ovary: is it inferior, or superior and deeply lobed?
At fruiting: four nutlets, a drupe/schizocarp, or a capsule/berry-like fruit?
Use square stems and aroma only as supporting clues.

comparison_matrix.first_lock: Opposite/decussate leaves usually without stipules; stems often 4-angled and foliage often aromatic.
comparison_matrix.break_the_tie: Superior ovary commonly deeply 4-lobed with a gynobasic style; fruit commonly four nutlets.
comparison_matrix.exception: Not every mint is aromatic, square-stemmed, bilabiate, or four-nutleted; Callicarpa is a conspicuous local breadth exception.

comparison_matrix.first_lock: Opposite leaves and often 4-angled stems can mimic Lamiaceae closely.
comparison_matrix.break_the_tie: Do not stop at the stem. Inspect ovary/style/fruit architecture; the classic deeply 4-lobed gynobasic mint ovary is not the default verbena pattern.
comparison_matrix.exception: Family boundaries historically shifted, so older references may place some genera differently.

comparison_matrix.first_lock: Opposite or whorled leaves can mimic mints/verbena vegetatively.
comparison_matrix.break_the_tie: Look BETWEEN opposite petioles for interpetiolar stipules, then confirm an inferior ovary when flowers/fruit allow.
comparison_matrix.exception: In Galium and relatives stipules can look leaflike, making the node appear whorled rather than simply opposite.

decision_key: Opposite leaves: inspect the node before the flower.
Distinct interpetiolar stipule or stipular sheath between petioles? → strong Rubiaceae door; seek inferior ovary confirmation.
No stipules: inspect the ovary/style and later fruit.
Deeply four-lobed superior ovary + style arising among/between lobes + four nutlets → strong Lamiaceae door.
Opposite-leaved Lamiales look-alike without that mint ovary/fruit package → keep Verbenaceae and other Lamiales open until reproductive characters resolve it.
